newsitem.title: CHILE: Storms cripple Chilean ports, block main highway.
newsitem.headline: Storms cripple Chilean ports, block main highway.

text.p: Severe storms forced Chilean authorities to close a sixth port, blocked the country's main highway and caused hundreds of people to flee their flooded homes, Chile's National Office of Emergencies (ONEMI) reported on Sunday.
An ONEMI official said the torrential rains and high winds caused the closing of the port of Coquimbo. Valparaiso, San Antonio, Quintana, Talcahuano and Lirquen had been shut down on Saturday.
The official said the ports, all of which are in Chile's central region, would remain closed until the weather improves, probably by Tuesday or Wednesday.
She added that the storms had not disrupted the northern ports that serve some of Chile's biggest copper mines.

The unusually heavy downpour caused flash flooding and mudslides in several areas of the central region. The PanAmerican highway was cut off at five points between Santiago and the seaside resort of La Serena to the north.
ONEMI said at least 949 people had been evacuated from their homes and hundreds more suffered property damage because of the floods.
In Valparaiso's port, the raging surf battered a moored Chilean-flagged ship, the Carlos Darwin, until it sank. In the city's steep hills, mudslides hit at least four houses.
In the Andes mountains, heavy snowfalls caused the closing of border crossings to neighboring Argentina.

The dismal weather probably played a part in this long weekend's high road accident death toll. Since Friday 20 people were killed in crashes and one woman was reported missing after her car fell in a rain-swollen pond.
